seoTitle: Saint Augustine Storybook for Children | The Restless Heart
seoDescription: Saint Augustine storybook for ages 6-12: ten illustrated pages about a boy from North Africa who searched for years, found God, and became the bishop of Hippo, with a family reflection.
intro: Follow a clever, restless boy from North Africa as he searches for years, finds what his heart wanted, and becomes a bishop. Read together, then listen.
shortAnswer: This ten-page Saint Augustine storybook for ages 6 to 12 follows Augustine from his boyhood in Tagaste to his years as bishop of Hippo, using the dates the Church records and scenes from his own Confessions. It ends with a narrated family reflection to share together.
summaryHtml:
Saint Augustine lived from 354 to 430 in Roman North Africa and Italy. His feast is August 28. Nine narrative pages end with a narrated family reflection.

What This Story Covers

  • A Boy in Tagaste
  • A Mother's Prayers
  • A Teacher with a Restless Heart
  • A Bishop Who Taught Him to Listen
  • Tomorrow, and Tomorrow
  • Take Up and Read
  • Baptized at Easter
  • A Bishop Among the Poor
  • The Psalms on the Wall
familyReadingHtml:
With a parent or caregiver, read Psalm 92:13. Talk about what it means to flourish like a palm tree or a cedar of Lebanon.

The final page offers a question, a Bible reading, a small action and a short prayer. A trusted adult can read it aloud and stop to talk about any part.
aboutHtml: Illustrations are imaginative composites, not portraits or eyewitness scenes. Augustine's life is well recorded, and several scenes here come from his own book, the Confessions, so the story says "he later wrote." The last page is a present-day scene. The story leaves out parts of his early life that are not for children.

faq.a: A bishop of Hippo in North Africa (354-430), remembered as one of the great teachers of the Church. His feast is August 28.
It follows Benedict XVI's account of his life and Augustine's own Confessions, and says so where a scene comes from his own writing.
Children ages 6 to 12, reading or listening with family. Ten illustrated pages end with a four-part family reflection.
